subject: SIG: SCIM sync edge cases + RBAC mapping clarification
messages:

Cc: Aurora Finance Security <security@aurorafin.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: SCIM incremental sync edge cases and RBAC mapping

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the SIG team had a couple of follow-up asks specific to SCIM behavior and RBAC that we need to address before the next evidence submission. TL;DR: we saw an intermittent "duplicate user" race during your SCIM incremental sync and we need the exact behavior notes and any logs you can pull for May 1-15.

Questions we need covered for the SIG:
- Does Redwood support incremental delta syncs vs full-replace for /Users? Behavior when an external identity provider (IdP) changes username/primaryEmail.
- How do you surface and resolve "orphaned" accounts when SCIM returns 404 on PATCH?
- Exact RBAC mapping applied at provisioning time (role -> Redwood role id mapping + default access on first provision) and whether we enforce least-privilege by default.
- MFA: are there any provisioning-time MFA exceptions or allow-lists?

Attachments: I attached the snippet we saw from our logs (scim_error_log_20260510.zip) — it shows a race where a PATCH returned 404 then a subsequent POST created a duplicate with a new id.

We need a concise written response we can include in the SIG evidence (ideally by end of week) and the raw provisioning logs for May 1-15. If any of this requires a short runbook or diagram, that would help the auditor review.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Zhou
Security Programs Manager | Aurora Finance
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhou <claire@aurorafin.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: SCIM incremental sync edge cases and RBAC mapping

Claire — thanks for the clear note and the log extract. Looping in Soojin (Security) for any audit wording and Marissa (Solutions) for provisioning diagrams.

High-level answers (we will turn into a tidy one-pager and include the requested logs):
- Incremental vs full-replace: Redwood's SCIM implementation supports incremental delta syncs out-of-the-box. By default we use PATCH/PUT for updates and rely on the IdP's externalId/email as the stable identifier; full-replace is available as a configuration option for customers who prefer reconciled state.
- Duplicate creation race: when a PATCH/PUT returns 404 we perform a subsequent POST create. We use a short, idempotent retry window (4 retries over 30s) and a dedupe check on externalId + primaryEmail before accepting a newly created user. That dedupe check is best-effort and can be configured to be strict (reject creates that conflict) — we will include the config flag and current tenant setting in the export.
- Orphaned accounts: we mark accounts as "orphaned_detached" when the IdP indicates deletion but the account has associated tokens/sessions; those accounts are soft-deleted and flagged for admin review. Auto-deprovisioning can be set to immediate delete (not recommended) or staged (default 7-day hold).
- RBAC mapping: provisioning applies role mappings defined in the SCIM service settings. By default the mapping assigns the minimal role required (viewer) and a post-provisioning automation can escalate to higher roles if matched by group rules. We'll export the current mapping for your tenant (CSV) and a sample of the role id -> permission list.
- MFA: no provisioning-time MFA exceptions in the platform. MFA enforcement is evaluated at auth time; you can configure org-level allow-lists for service accounts (not user accounts).

Attachments: I attached a short diagram of our provisioning flow (scim-provisioning-diagram.pdf) and will pull the May 1-15 sync logs and the mapping CSV. If you can confirm whether the auditor needs API-level traces (x-request-id) or sanitized logs, we'll prioritize accordingly.

Next steps:
- Soojin: can you craft a SIG-friendly paragraph (2-3 bullets) for "How we prevent duplicate users and orphaned accounts"?
- Marissa: please add the mapping CSV and a sample role matrix to the export.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call if that helps.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Product Security Manager | Redwood Inference

Thanks Mina — that is helpful. For the SIG pack the auditor specifically asked for:
1) Raw provisioning traces (API request/response pairs) with x-request-ids for May 1-15 — we will need them sanitized for PII but with IDs preserved so they can match the error sequence.
2) The tenant's SCIM mapping CSV and a short note stating the default post-provision role.
3) A short paragraph confirming the default soft-delete window and the policy when tokens/sessions exist.

Attached an audit intake form (audit_request_form.pdf) that lists the format and redaction guidance. SIG timeline: final evidence in two weeks, so timing is tight. Can you confirm if you can produce the sanitized traces by end of week? If not, we can schedule a short call to walk through samples.

Claire

Claire — thanks, committed to delivering the sanitized traces and mapping CSV. Quick clarifications inline and a couple of sample lines from the SCIM export below to show how we record externalId and idempotency.

- Traces: we can produce request/response pairs with all headers and bodies redacted for PII except x-request-id, externalId, and error codes. ETA: end of day Friday (26 May).
- Mapping CSV: will include columns (group_name, scim_group_id, redwood_role_id, assigned_permissions) and an example row.
- Soft-delete policy: default is 7-day hold for deprovisioned users; if a user has active tokens we set state to orphaned_detached and the account remains in read-only for 30 days unless an admin opts to purge earlier.

Sample SCIM export (sanitized lines):
> id: 6f4b2a9b
> externalId: aurora|jdoe
> userName: jdoe@aurorafin.com
> active: false
> meta.lastModified: 2026-05-10T14:22:30Z

> id: 6f4b3c1d
> externalId: aurora|mjensen
> userName: mjensen@aurorafin.com
> active: true
> meta.lastModified: 2026-05-12T08:11:12Z

Attachments included in the export: scim_sample_export_lines.txt (small), provisioning_traces_may1-15_sanitized.zip (will be uploaded via secure link).

If helpful I'll schedule a 30-min handoff with your audit lead to walk the traces and confirm redaction. Which timezone is the auditor in?
